findings.finding: Two complete board-making lines in Asia were explicitly booked into Q3 2026 orders received (coated board line, released 2026-09-23; Anhui Linping PM 9, released 2026-10-12, Inderes estimate ~EUR 100m), Severn adds orders from 1 July, and the Q3 2025 comparison base was a weak EUR 1,083m, so Q3 orders should come in at or above the ~EUR 1.2bn consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Orders drove the last prints: Q1'26 orders -18% with an EBITA miss, stock -8.5% (2026-04-28); Q2'25 orders +19% beat, +11.9% (2025-07-23); Q2'26 orders -10% but EBITA beat plus strategic review, +22.1% (2026-07-24). Observed on Yahoo daily closes on the real report dates.
findings.original_quote: Inderes (da): "Det er dog allerede den anden ret store ordre på kartonmaskiner fra Asien i Q3" - 'it is already the second fairly large board-machine order from Asia in Q3'
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: both orders are public and Inderes, who knows them, still estimates ~1.2bn slightly BELOW consensus. What is not priced is the total - services and Process Efficiency intake are unannounced. If the market had priced an order beat the stock would not have drifted -5.75% over 20 sessions into the print; it did. Sized small because the decisive part is public.

findings.finding: Cost actions should support Q3 margin against a consensus that assumes only flat margin (12.3% vs 12.3%): Q2 comparable EBITA beat consensus (152m vs ~140m) with comparable SG&A EUR 79m below FY2024, and ~2,400 Finnish employees are on temporary layoffs of up to 90 days between June and December.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EBITA surprises moved it hard both ways: Q1'26 miss (114 vs 125) -8.5%; Q2'26 beat (152 vs 140) +22.1% (with the review); Q4'25 strong profitability but cautious guide -8.6%.
findings.original_quote: "Yhtiö lomauttaa Suomessa noin 2 400 työntekijää." / "Lomautukset kestävät enintään 90 päivää, ja ne toteutetaan kesäkuun ja joulukuun lopun välisenä aikana." - 'The company is temporarily laying off about 2,400 employees in Finland... up to 90 days, carried out between June and the end of December.'
findings.why_not_priced: Inference from public cost facts, not a sourced Q3 number. The layoff reason ('paperi- ja kartonkikonemarkkinoiden heikko kysyntä', weak paper/board machine demand) also argues for weaker project sales, and Inderes names mix, inflation and pricing as margin limits, so the net is small. If priced as a beat, consensus margin would sit above last year's 12.3%; it sits on it.

findings.finding: The guide is low against consensus on both lines: FY sales guided 'at the 2025 level (5,197m)' while Inderes carries 5,404m (+4%, Severn consolidating from July), and FY comparable EBITA guided at or above 620m where H1 266m plus Q3 consensus 163m leaves Q4 needing only ~191m against 196m a year ago, so a reiteration is safe and any tightening upward is possible.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4'25 release (2026-02-06) gave a 'cautious' 2026 guide that overshadowed strong profitability and the stock fell 8.6%; reiterations in Q1 and Q2 2026 did not drive the moves.
findings.original_quote: "vuoden 2026 liikevaihto pysyy vuoden 2025 tasolla (5 197 milj. euroa)" / "vertailukelpoinen EBITA vuonna 2026 pysyy edellisvuoden tasolla tai kasvaa verrattuna vuoteen 2025 (620 milj. euroa)"
findings.why_not_priced: Inderes's preview (22.10.2026) says it expects Valmet to repeat the guidance (paraphrased; exact Finnish sentence not captured), so a raise is not in the preview; consensus already sits above the sales guide, so a sales raise would only confirm the numbers, which is why this is small. If a raise were priced, the stock would not be 5.75% off its 20-day level into the print.

findings.original_quote: "Lähi-idän tilanteen vaikutus öljy- ja kaasusektorin kysyntään on luultavasti estänyt tuntuvamman orgaanisen kasvun" - 'the Middle East situation's effect on oil and gas demand has probably prevented more noticeable organic growth'
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: it sits inside Inderes's estimate, which is close to consensus. The one-offs are explicitly outside consensus, so a reported-EPS miss on integration costs is a small unpriced risk; comparable EBITA, the line that moves the stock, excludes them.
